svg.title: X and yaw from the turn geometry
svg.desc: Four steps. One reading puts the sensor somewhere on a circle centred on the rear-axle line, heading included. Walking along that circle trades lever arm against yaw, so each turn is one line in the yaw versus lever-arm plane. Several turns give lines that cross in one small region. The estimate is the point with the smallest weighted squared gap to all eleven lines of one A2D2 drive.
svg.text: Where can the sensor be? The turn geometry answers it.
A2D2 FRONT_CENTER · 11 gated turns · 697 samples · one sensor at a time, no cross-sensor matching
One reading
The mount lies on a circle centred on the rear-axle
line — position and heading together.
Circle → line
Walking the circle trades lever arm against yaw:
one turn draws one line in the (ψ, pₓ) plane.
More turns
Turns of different radius and sign give lines
that cross in one small region.
Least squares
The lines do not meet exactly; the estimate is the
point of smallest weighted squared gap to all of them.
On the vehicle (top view)
turn radii and angles compressed for legibility

g.text: Radius is fixed by the reading: R = |ṽ| / ω; the centre is
the instantaneous centre of rotation, on the rear-axle line.
Every candidate reads the same velocity in its own frame,
so heading turns with position — one reading pins neither.
Walk along the circle: the lever arm pₓ and the yaw ψ
move together, one against the other.
That trade-off is the line drawn on the right.
Three turns, three circles, all through the true mount.
Pick a trial yaw and each turn names its own pₓ;
they agree at one yaw only.
Height along the axle line is still open: it depends on the
body speed, which this stage never uses. py is settled later.

svg.text: In the (ψ, pₓ) plane — real turns
each line is one gated turn of the drive; axes are real units
mounting yaw ψ [deg]

g.text: three turns already box it in

svg.text: gap read along pₓ, weighted by turn rate and sample count
